title: Summed Walsh orthogonality for the mod-2 inner product
statement:
Fix $n \in \bbn$. For a Boolean value $b$, let $\varepsilon(b) \in \{\pm 1\}$ denote its Boolean sign, equal to $+1$ when $b$ is $\mathrm{false}$ and $-1$ when $b$ is $\mathrm{true}$; and for $n$-bit Boolean inputs $x, y$, let $\langle x, y\rangle$ denote their mod-2 inner product (which is $\mathrm{true}$ exactly when the number of coordinates $i$ with $x_i = y_i = \mathrm{true}$ is odd). Then for any two $n$-bit Boolean inputs $y$ and $z$,
\[
  \sum_{x} \varepsilon\bigl(\langle x, y\rangle\bigr)\,\varepsilon\bigl(\langle x, z\rangle\bigr)
  = \begin{cases} 2^n & \text{if } y = z, \\ 0 & \text{if } y \neq z, \end{cases}
\]
where the sum ranges over all $2^n$ Boolean inputs $x$.
hypotheses_covered: y and z are arbitrary n-bit Boolean inputs (no side conditions)
